value: bimodal (most active individuals late morning and afternoon)
method: hourly frequency of active lizards, from capture times of free-living lizards caught by hand or noose between 10:00 and 19:00 h; Pearson chi-square on hourly frequencies
conditions: Free-living lizards at Quebrada Vallecito (Calingasta Department, San Juan Province, Argentina; type locality of the species), sampled in October 2008, December 2008 and April 2009; the paper does not say whether the three months were pooled for the hourly pattern. 84 P. williamsi were captured at the site (27 males, 40 females, 17 juveniles); the n used in the hourly analysis is not stated in the text read. Activity was inferred from the times lizards were caught active (10:00-19:00 h), not from continuous observation. The same paragraph reports activity over 7 hours (11:00-18:00 h) with fewer lizards than expected at 13:00-14:00 h (chi-square P < 0.0001); the syntopic Liolaemus parvus at the same site was unimodal. The paper also measured preferred body temperature in a laboratory gradient, which is not part of this record.
